clue.text: One floundering round the floor? Not her!

definitions.text: One floundering round the floor? Not her!

parts.words: One floundering round the floor? Not her!
parts.note: describes, by contrast, the person at a dance who never gets onto the floor at all but sits out every number at the side of the room

explanation.definitionFit: A woman left sitting by the wall at a dance, never asked to partner anyone, is the classic shy non-dancer the term names.

clue.text: A lotion for waves

definitions.meaning: a medicated liquid applied to the skin, as in an eyewash
the disturbed water left behind a moving boat

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a soothing liquid for bathing skin or eyes and the swell churned up in a vessel's wake.

clue.text: Smaller bed occupied by student

indicators.note: the bed has someone lodged in it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: litter is straw or bedding laid down for animals
L is the learner driver's plate letter, a standard abbreviation for student

explanation.surface: A bed gets cramped once a student moves in.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial comparative of 'little', meaning of reduced size.

clue.text: New car should have this before starting a rally, perhaps

definitions.text: New car should have this before starting a rally, perhaps

parts.words: New car should have this before starting a rally, perhaps
parts.note: reads as motoring advice about a check-up for a vehicle before a road race, but a rally is also an exchange of shots in tennis, which begins with the opening serve

explanation.walkthrough: The car meaning is the first maintenance check after purchase; in tennis a rally is opened by the server's first attempt to put the ball in play.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the garage's initial check-up on a new vehicle and the opening serve in a tennis point go by this phrase.

clue.text: It's no distance on the line to the fruit-growing area

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, stands for no or nothing
a range is a distance, as in the range of a gun
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the garden's fruit house is only a short hop down the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A glasshouse built for raising citrus trees, so a sheltered place for cultivating fruit.

clue.text: Confusing in game or puzzle

indicators.note: the letters are muddled up, as a confusing arrangement would be

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a board game baffling, or simply a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or mystery is something baffling that resists understanding.

clue.text: Take spoonfuls out of the duck consomme

indicators.note: the sipping word sits outside the duck letter, holding it within

parts.note: to sup is to take liquid a spoonful or sip at a time
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written O

explanation.surface: A diner is told to spoon up some clear broth made from duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, so O; 'out of' is read as SUP being on the outside of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Consomme is a clear broth, one kind of that liquid first course.

clue.text: Needle is available — order silk material

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

indicators.note: the silk is treated as raw stuff to be worked up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert offers needles in stock, alongside silk fabric to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' signals the rearrangement of SILK to LISK; 'is available' just links. A needle is a tall pointed stone pillar, like Cleopatra's Needle in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is called a needle, as with Cleopatra's Needle on the Thames.

clue.text: Final examination

parts.note: looks like the last paper of a degree course but means the inspection of a body after death, the last check anyone undergoes

explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is the last inspection a person ever receives, carried out after they have died.

clue.text: Drunken Australian's wild revelry

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An inebriated man from Down Under parties hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges AUSTRALIAN; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman midwinter festival gave its name to any unrestrained orgy of merrymaking.

clue.text: Where officers eat pickle

definitions.meaning: the dining room for military officers
a predicament or muddle, as in being in a pickle

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an armed forces dining hall and a sorry plight or jam.

clue.text: Sweet that comes with instructions on cooking

definitions.text: Sweet that comes with instructions on cooking

parts.words: Sweet that comes with instructions on cooking
parts.note: a dessert whose name begins with a two-word baking command, telling the cook to do the job properly

explanation.walkthrough: This is a British almond-and-jam pastry from Bakewell in Derbyshire; its name starts with what looks like an order to the cook.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond and jam pastry is a classic British pudding, and its first word reads like a baking direction.

clue.text: Flier without a single chart

indicators.note: one piece is taken away from the flier word

parts.note: a pilot flies an aircraft
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An airman has lost his only map.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot is to mark out a course on a map, so it can mean to chart.

clue.text: I'm amusing my form in place of exercises

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A speaker boasts that they keep their schoolmates entertained when they should be doing PE.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' reshapes AMUSING MY; 'I'm' and 'in' just link. 'Form' also suggests a school class, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym is a hall fitted out for physical training and drills.

clue.text: Compensation for bad printing

definitions.meaning: balancing one thing against another to cancel it out
the fault where wet ink from one sheet marks the back of the next

explanation.definitionFit: The word means counterbalancing a loss, and also the smudging transfer of ink between freshly printed sheets.

clue.text: Declines an extra visitor, say, for Goldilocks?

definitions.meaning: refrains or holds back from doing something

definitions.text: an extra visitor, say, for Goldilocks?
definitions.meaning: in the fairy tale the girl turns up uninvited at the home of the three animals, so she was a surplus guest for them

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the second reading: Goldilocks was an unexpected guest at the cottage of the three bears.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to abstain or decline to act; split in two the word names who the fairy-tale girl visited.

clue.text: Cup with wide mouth used by very old folk

definitions.text: Cup with wide mouth used by very old folk

parts.words: Cup with wide mouth used by very old folk
parts.note: a broad-lipped drinking vessel, also the pottery that names a prehistoric Bronze Age people

explanation.walkthrough: The 'very old folk' are the Bronze Age people archaeologists name after their distinctive bell-shaped pottery drinking vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-mouthed drinking vessel, and the pottery type that gives the prehistoric Bell Beaker culture its name.

clue.text: No task for a failure

parts.note: O, the zero figure, stands for none
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: Without an assignment, someone feels like a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a failure to do something, a thing left undone.

clue.text: Liner requiring record cover

definitions.meaning: a tube fitted inside another, as in an engine cylinder
the card jacket a vinyl disc is kept in

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tubular lining fitted inside a part and the cardboard jacket of a vinyl album.

clue.text: Patent is incontestable

definitions.meaning: obvious or plain, as in a patent lie

explanation.definitionFit: Something patent is plainly obvious, and something beyond dispute is clearly so: both are senses of manifest.

clue.text: The current strength is a master for each period

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA, Master of Arts
per means for each, as in per head
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone claims that today's might belongs to one ruler in every era.
explanation.definitionFit: The strength of an electric current is measured in amps, so a flow's magnitude is this.

clue.text: Publicise boost for emergency transport

parts.note: to air views is to make them public
a lift is a boost, as in a morale lift

explanation.surface: Advertising gives a welcome push to relief flights.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief operation flying supplies or people out by aircraft when roads are cut off.

clue.text: Couple again in 'resort

definitions.meaning: to join two things together once more, a second pairing
to go or betake oneself somewhere, as in resorting to a place

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-PAIR for the first sense; for the second, 'repair to the bar' means go there. The scan prints a plain 'in resort'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it means to pair up a second time; whole it is the old verb to go or betake oneself somewhere.

clue.text: Bird watchers who get the fidgets?

definitions.meaning: enthusiasts who chase sightings of rare birds

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for keen birders who rush after rarities, and literally people prone to nervous jerks.

clue.text: Bait left by the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An angler leaves bait on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is a decoy used to attract fish, the same job bait does.

clue.text: Hide in mountain

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with its hair
a hill or high moorland, especially in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an animal's pelt, and in the north of England an upland hill such as those of the Lake District.

clue.text: The fish lie back in the sediment

indicators.note: the letters lie in reverse, read from right to left
the letters are found tucked inside the following word

explanation.surface: Some fish are resting on their backs in the mud at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Within 'sediment' lies SEDI; 'back' turns it to give the plural of the ide, a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater carp-family species; this is its plural, so a group of those fish.

clue.text: I more than once said: "Convert assets into money"

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken out loud, so what is heard matters, not how it is written

parts.note: the letter I, always written as a capital, taken several times: capital I's

explanation.surface: A speaker keeps repeating a piece of financial advice about cashing in.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronoun I is always written in upper case, so several of them are 'capital I's', which spoken sounds like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitalise holdings is to realise them, turning property or stock into cash.

clue.text: The guns find the monarch of the glen in retreat

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: The Monarch of the Glen is Landseer's famous painting of a red deer stag

explanation.surface: Hunters with rifles find the lordly red deer fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monarch of the Glen is a famous Victorian painting of a Highland red deer stag. Gats are gangsters' pistols, from Gatling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gat is old slang for a handgun, so these are pistols or firearms.

clue.text: Add on 1,000 — almost the whole final sum

indicators.note: the adding word is placed on after the thousand, following it

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
to tot up is to add

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: all means the whole

explanation.surface: An accountant tacks a thousand onto nearly everything for the bottom line.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed reads '£1,000', a grand; ALL loses its last letter to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: The overall amount at the foot of a column of figures is the complete total.
